audit_findings.title: Potential equity-cash-flow and enterprise-bridge mismatch
audit_findings.mechanism: If OE is an equity-level cash flow, removing the duplicated debt deduction would increase the equity bridge by $100.124 million.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company paid cash for interest of $ 15.8 million, $ 7.7 million, and $ 1.6 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023 , respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The exact OE formula is absent, so double counting is possible rather than demonstrated. Even if the entire debt deduction were erroneous, base value would rise only from $133.83 to about $137.57 per share, still far below the $332.04 market price; the valuation conclusion would not change.
audit_findings.action: Trace the OE formula for interest treatment. If after-tax interest was not added back, rerun the bridge without the $100.124 million debt deduction; otherwise retain the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Maintenance capital expenditure may be materially understated
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed net capital expenditures were $544.1 million in 2025 and forecast at $350 million to $400 million for 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Any understatement of recurring maintenance capex directly overstates the $256.1 million OE anchor and every forecast and terminal cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: Our net capital expenditures for 2025 were approximately $544 million and we anticipate net capital expenditures in 2026 of approximately $350 million to $400 million, subject to the ongoing evaluation of market conditions.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved classification issue, not a demonstrated error, because total capex includes expansion. Nevertheless, Saia describes the business as highly capital intensive, and the filed spending amounts exceed the OE anchor. A materially higher sustainable maintenance requirement could substantially reduce or eliminate normalized OE and therefore is capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the maintenance deduction by asset class and replacement cycle, including fleet age, terminal refurbishment, technology renewal, asset-sale proceeds and the capital required to sustain forecast network capacity; then rerun all scenarios using the supported maintenance amount.

audit_findings.title: Exceptional cash-tax deferral may be capitalized as recurring earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $65.308 million deferred tax expense, equal to 25.5% of the $256.1 million anchor; 2025 cash taxes were $76.253 million below the $82.353 million tax provision
audit_findings.mechanism: If OE uses operating cash flow without normalizing taxes, deferred tax expense is added back and the unusually low cash payment can inflate the anchor and terminal cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company paid cash for income taxes of $ 6.1 million, $ 101.2 million, and $ 72.8 million in 2025, 2024 and 2023 , respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large 2025 tax deferral but does not establish how the OE calculation treated it or when it will reverse. At 25.5% of the anchor, the deferred-tax amount is large enough to materially alter the valuation if capitalized as recurring owner earnings.
audit_findings.action: Trace taxes through the OE calculation, reconcile the $65.308 million deferred provision to depreciation-related temporary differences, estimate reversal timing under the forecast capex path, and rerun using a sustainable cash-tax burden.

audit_findings.title: Long-tail self-insurance claims may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; latest filed claims and insurance liabilities were $113.2 million, equivalent to $4.23 per share if wholly treated as an incremental bridge claim
audit_findings.mechanism: An incremental runoff or under-reserved obligation would reduce the equity bridge or future OE, while normal recurring claims expense and reserve settlements may already be captured in earnings and working-capital cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: These liabilities are recorded within claims and insurance accruals (current) of $46.0 million, and claims, insurance, and other (non-current) of $79.1 million, as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The reserve is demonstrated, but its omission from the debt bridge is not itself an error because it is an operating liability and claims expense is already recognized. The latest reserve declined from $125.1 million at year-end to $113.2 million, and the filing provides no quantified adverse development. Materiality remains unresolved because any under-reservation or abnormal runoff is unquantified and the OE working-capital treatment is unknown.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the latest $113.2 million reserve by accident year and claim type, obtain actuarial development and paid-loss data, and trace reserve changes and settlements through OE before deciding whether an incremental runoff deduction is required.

audit_findings.title: The latest anchor may retain a nonrecurring property-sale benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.4 million terminal-sale gain, partly offset by a $1.9 million impairment; filed net property-disposal gain was $12.458 million, or 4.9% of the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: An unremoved disposal gain would overstate the OE anchor and would be compounded through forecast and terminal growth; sale proceeds could also improperly reduce maintenance capex.
audit_findings.evidence: Operating (gains) losses, net decreased $16.9 million in 2025 compared to 2024 due to a gain on the sale of a terminal of $16.4 million, partially offset by a real estate impairment loss of $1.9 million.
audit_findings.explanation: Inclusion in OE is possible rather than demonstrated because the OE formula is not supplied. Even if the full $12.458 million net property-disposal gain were removed from the anchor and the DCF moved proportionally, base value would fall by about $6.53 per share, from $133.83 to roughly $127.30, leaving the conclusion versus the $332.04 market price unchanged.
audit_findings.action: Trace the gain, impairment and $23.511 million of total property-disposal proceeds through OE and maintenance capex; remove any included nonrecurring benefit in the next rerun.

audit_findings.title: Deferred director share claims may be missing from the denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: 104,399 shares, equal to 0.39% of the 26.766846 million-share denominator and approximately $0.52 per base-value share in the worst case
audit_findings.mechanism: Any omitted deferred director units would increase fully diluted shares and reduce value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company had 104,399 and 101,951 shares reserved for issuance under the Directors’ Deferred Fee Plan at December 31, 2025 and 2024 , respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The 10-K states that these reserved director shares are treated as common stock in computing basic EPS, so omission is not demonstrated. Even if all 104,399 shares were additionally missing, base value would decline only from $133.83 to approximately $133.30 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the point-in-time fully diluted denominator to basic shares, deferred director units, restricted shares and performance awards; add only units not already included in the reported or constructed share count.
